title: Linux security primitives
subtitle: Container limits, path safety, shell allow-lists, UID pinning and egress control are the floor under my agent runtime, not an afterthought.

stats.label: commits by the coding agent's worker to the main repository

lede: Agent Swarm: every new agent tends to arrive with its own idea of what it may touch. I wanted the isolation floor declared once, as data, and inherited by every agent class. Each persona in the catalog carries a sandbox section, so a new agent class gets the floor without new code. The persona launcher starts one container per persona with a scoped token, a workspace and a budget. Inside the runtime, the frozen tool pipeline enforces per-call resource quotas read from procfs, and timeouts, before any tool body runs. The trust plane refuses connection strings that are not TLS. I tested the floor with a coding agent on a local open-weight model.
quote: On a single host the kernel already knows who is calling, so I check peer credentials on local sockets and keep shared secrets off that path.
evidence: Sandboxing and container hardening: per-persona sandboxes declaring container limits, workspace type and shell allow and deny patterns, inherited by every agent class.
Linux security primitives: cross-user message delivery through a socket-activated Unix socket checked with kernel peer credentials, with no shared secrets on that path.
Least privilege for AI agents: a coding agent that pushed from a throwaway container under a shell allow-list and made 0 commits to the main repository.
author: Corey James
